217:317.description:
The button: Base UI's, so `focusableWhenDisabled` and `render` work, styled by variant and size. An icon goes in as a child, before or after the label, and so does a `Kbd variant="button"`; an icon-only button takes `iconOnly` and needs an `aria-label`. It is `type="button"` unless told otherwise, so one inside a form doesn't submit it by accident.

To make another component look like a button — a toolbar item, a number field's stepper — give it `getButtonClassName` instead; to make a Base UI trigger one, pass this as its `render`.

variant:
- pop: The accent, solid, as a checked checkbox or switch is: the primary action of the whole surface. At most one per surface: if two things pop, neither does.
- gray: Solid gray ground. Lifts a button above the ones around it without spending color — a highlight, not a primary action.
- outline: The default. A ghost with an edge, for a button on open ground where nothing else marks it as a target. Ranks equally with `ghost`: mixing the two in one group separates kinds of control (the PR toolbar outlines its Auto-merge toggle among ghost actions), never levels of importance.
- outline-inverted: `outline` for a button on an inverted ground — a selected row, not dark mode.
- danger: For an act the user cannot take back: deleting, discarding, hard-resetting. Chosen by consequence, so it sits outside the ladder.
- danger-solid: `danger` at full strength, for the answer to a confirmation that destroys something.
- ghost: No ground, no border. For actions inside something already a container: a row, a toolbar, a popup.
- ghost-inverted: `ghost` for a button on an inverted ground — a selected row, not dark mode.

In Figma: `state` is the drawing's only: hover is the button under the pointer, which the code draws from CSS rather than a prop.

One row: an optional `leading` picture or checkbox, a `title` with its `icon`, light (`online`) and `badge`, an optional `description` and `meta`, and what ends the row (`trailing`). For list items, card rows, machines, repositories and settings; several go in a RowGroup, which draws the lines between them.

`trailing` sits on the title's line: `"chevron"` on a row that opens something, or the control itself (a `Switch`, a tick, a `Button`). Leave it out on a plain row.

A row that does something is the whole click target, through `render`: an `<a href>` or a `<button>` for a row that opens something, a `<label htmlFor>` the trailing `Switch`'s `id` for a setting, so a click anywhere on the row flips it. Then it tints under the pointer and draws the focus ring, the label's while its switch has keyboard focus. A row that renders as a `<div>`, the default, is static: a control in it answers on its own.

`disabled` fades the row to half on the grey ground and stops it answering the pointer; it doesn't disable what the row renders, so pass `disabled` to the `<button>` or the `Switch` too, or leave out the link's `href`. A disabled control inside doesn't fade a second time. Say why in the `description`.

2572:3286.description:
A glyph and a short value in a row's meta: a count, an age, a branch's name. The type sets both. Amber is work waiting on you (`behind`, `uncommitted`, `agent-waiting`), blue is work to send (`unpushed`), green is an agent at work (`agent-working`); the rest are neutral, `stack` among them: where a branch sits in its stack, "1/3 in stack". `rebased` is the unpushed arrow in that neutral grey: commits that were pushed and have been rewritten since, most often by a rebase onto the target, so a push replaces them rather than sending new work. Red is what can't go on until you step in: `conflicts`, how many of a branch's commits are conflicted. Quietest of all are `empty`, a branch with no commits yet, and `head`, what a worktree with nothing to list is on (`empty`, `detached`); a row shows either first, ahead of its counts. `cpu` is a process's CPU use while it stays low, in green; `cpu-danger` is the same use once it runs high, in red with a warning on the chip.

The value is the children, so a host formats it (`12`, `3d`, `retry-transfers`). The glyph says nothing to a screen reader: wrap the count in a `Tooltip` saying what it counts, or give it an `aria-label`. A long value, such as a branch's name, ends in an ellipsis once its row runs out of room.

With `onPress` the count is the button for its next step: ↓ `behind` updates, ↑ `unpushed` pushes. It looks the same at rest and takes up the same room; under the pointer it sits on its own colour at 14% (a grey one on the hover ground) and keeps its text, and keyboard focus shows the ring. Its `Tooltip` then says what pressing it does ("Push 4 commits"), not what it counts. The row under it still gets the click, so a host that selects rows stops it there. `onPress` rather than `onClick`, because a `Tooltip` hands its trigger an `onClick` of its own: a count that only explains itself on hover stays a plain count.

In Figma: `state=hover` is the drawing's only: what it draws under the pointer when it has `onPress`.

Rules: https://github.com/gitbutlerapp/gitbutler/blob/master/packages/but-ui/design/components/meta-lines.md

The trigger is a field-sized outline button reading the current choice, led by that choice's icon or image if it has one, and the list it opens is the same Popup every dropdown wears, with a tick on the row that is chosen now.

2572:3458.description:
A branch in the sidebar. With a pull request (`pr`), the row is the request: its state in the glyph and the badge, its number, and its title as `title`; without one, `title` is the branch's name.

Its `meta` reads in one order: `conflicts`, then `CiStatus`, ↓ `behind`, ↑ `unpushed`, `uncommitted`, and `commits`. `conflicts` counts its conflicted commits while it is folded; on an expanded branch drop it, since each CommitItem marks its own. Show ↑ or ⟜, never both; on an expanded branch drop ⟜, since its commits are listed under it. A branch with no commits yet leads with `empty` saying "empty", so its row isn't bare. `actions` hold the one next step (Resolve, Update, Push, Create PR or Merge), then View PR on a branch with a request.

A merged request is done with: its title recedes. A branch merged into its target with no request known takes `merged`: the same muted title, its branch glyph and a Merged badge.

While an action on the branch runs, its `busy` spinner takes the glyph's colour. A merge takes `pr` state `merged` as it starts, so the row reads as where it is heading; back to `open` if it is refused.

Under the pointer, on keyboard focus and while selected, its state stays and the menu follows it at once, while the name gives way. An action takes the state's place under the pointer only; selected, the state stays.

In Figma: `pr` follows the pull request: `none` shows the branch's name, the others its number and title, and `none-merged` is `merged` with no request known. The counts come from BranchMeta: on an expanded branch turn off commits (⟜), and turn on conflicts only while it's folded. For a branch with no commits yet, turn on commits alone and set its text to empty.

Rules: https://github.com/gitbutlerapp/gitbutler/blob/master/packages/but-ui/design/components/sidebar-trees.md

2210:1708.description:
One line of consequence, floated over the surface that caused it: a glyph, a sentence, and at most one button, fenced off behind a divider: Undo when what just happened can be taken back, or a close button when the snackbar waits to be dismissed by hand. Never both: an undoable snackbar leaves on its own, so it has nothing to close. A whole Toasts card would state a title and a description; a snackbar has only the sentence, so it can sit close to the thing it is about rather than in the corner of the window.

Every variant wears the same surface: the verdict is carried by the glyph alone, so a run of snackbars reads as one row of statements rather than a traffic light.

variant:
- info: Something happened worth saying, with no verdict attached.
- warning: An act that came off with a catch: it ran, but not quite as asked.
- danger: An act that failed, or refused to run.
- safe: An act that came off.
